skip_reason: Post-move complaint/damages call, not a sales or quoting call. Customer Matthew Bowen (already moved) calls to report a long list of problems: two broken TVs, damaged wood furniture, missing bed hardware and shelving glass, belongings still left behind in Austin, and a final price that came in far above the original estimate ($2,600 quoted vs. roughly $6,200 charged). He asks for a $2,500 refund and wants Frank (branch manager) to call him back. Garrison is just taking notes and passing everything to Frank — no move is being priced or booked on this call.
phone_presence_notes: Garrison stays calm and apologetic through a long, profanity-laced complaint and validates the customer's frustration repeatedly ("those frustrations are all absolutely valid"), but leans heavily on repetitive filler ("right," "yeah, yeah") and only uses the customer's name once, at the very top of the call.
